proposed_comments.title: Do not show multi-item counters for ordinary Explorer activation
proposed_comments.body:
### Do not show multi-item counters for ordinary Explorer activation

**Severity:** `high`

`Items` contains the whole neighboring directory for Explorer activation, so using `Items.Count > 1` makes the title bar show an index/total counter even when the user selected one file. The previous behavior only showed that counter for true multi-selection. Track activation multiplicity separately: use `NeighboringItemsQuery.IsMultipleFilesActivation` for Explorer and `paths.Count > 1` for CLI.

```suggestion
        [ObservableProperty]
        [NotifyPropertyChangedFor(nameof(DisplayItemCount))]
        [NotifyPropertyChangedFor(nameof(HasMultipleItems))]
        private IReadOnlyList<IFileSystemItem>? _items;

        [ObservableProperty]
        [NotifyPropertyChangedFor(nameof(HasMultipleItems))]
        private bool _isMultipleItemsActivation;
```

confidence.rationale: The reviewed code replaced the old IsMultipleFilesActivation condition with Items.Count, which is known to include neighbors for single Explorer activation.

proposed_comments.title: Add end-to-end coverage for the direct CLI launch path
proposed_comments.body:
### Add end-to-end coverage for the direct CLI launch path

**Severity:** `medium`

The new unit tests cover argument classification, but the core direct-CLI workflow still has no regression test that launches Peek with multiple paths and verifies relative-path expansion, mixed file/folder item creation, navigation, and invalid-input exit behavior. Please extend the Peek UI test coverage for the CLI activation path so these cross-process regressions are observable.

confidence.rationale: Existing tests cover classifier and Explorer activation, while the direct CLI launch branch is a separate cross-process path.
